news.title: Nigeria in the Quagmire of Being Unable to Host World Cup - Infantino
news.lede: Nigeria, 24 November 2026 - Nigeria, 23 November 2026 – FIFA President Gianni Infantino has spoken a bitter truth to Nigerian authorities, especially those responsible for ensuring that the country has state-of-the-art sports infrastructure, along with supportive and related infrastructure, that meets recommended international standards. He told ARISE News in Abuja that Nigeria, as it stands now, could not host a FIFA World Cup. "Today, no," Infantino said during the interview, in which he went further to cite inadequate infrastructure as the reason. Infantino is himself a man under siege.

news.title: Wales women: Home World Cup to inspire ' future stars - Wilkinson
news.lede: Rhian Wilkinson was appointed Wales head coach in February 2024. Wales head coach Rhian Wilkinson says the prospect of a home Women's World Cup in 2035 can inspire a generation of young Welsh players. The Football Association of Wales (FAW) launched its new women's and girls' 10-year football strategy on Tuesday, less than 24 hours after Wales - along with England, Scotland and Northern Ireland - were confirmed as co-hosts of the 2035 Women's World Cup. Cardiff and Wrexham are both proposed host cities.

news.title: Wild Scenes As Dwarf Football World Cup Match Between Morocco & Colombia Erupts Into All-Out Brawl [VIDEO]
news.lede: Dwarf Football players (Photo via Twitter) The 2026 Short Stature World Cup, also known as the Dwarf Football World Cup, is gaining headlines this week. Unfortunately, it is not for the sport itself. It is taking place in Rabat, Morocco, running from late November through November 30, 2026. Governed by the Federación Internacional de Fútbol de Talla Baja, the sport features 7 players per side on a standard futsal court.

news.title: Jamaica joins US, Mexico and Costa Rica in landmark 2031 World Cup hosting role
news.lede: Jamaica has secured a landmark place in international football history, becoming part of a four-nation partnership to host the 2031 FIFA Women's World Cup and paving the way for the Reggae Girlz to automatically qualify for the expanded 48-team tournament. The announcement, confirmed by FIFA President Gianni Infantino at the organization's Congress in Zurich, Switzerland, on Monday, places Jamaica alongside the United States, Mexico and Costa Rica as co-hosts of the global showpiece. The historic achievement marks the first time a Caribbean nation will host matches at a senior FIFA World Cup, opening an unprecedented opportunity for Jamaica to showcase its football infrastructure, sporting ambitions, culture and hospitality to a worldwide audience.
